8 I am the LORD: that is my name: and my glory will I not give to another, neither my praise to graven images. (Isaiah 42:8 KJV)

Godâ€™s name is Lord, that is His name, not just a title. During the Old Testament days, God has referred to Himself with several different names. Here He says His name is Lord, and that is why we call Him Lord God, as He is God and His name is Lord.

This illustrates that when we call Jesus, Lord Jesus, we are calling Him both God and Jesus. This shows again how Jesus was God in the flesh (John 1:14) and not just another Prophet. Also note that the Lord says He will not give His Glory to another, and since the Bible tells us that Jesus was the Glory of God (Matthew 16:27), it again shows that Jesus was God. This is hard for man to understand, but we have to accept the fact that the Father, Jesus the Son, and the Holy Ghost are all one God. We call this the Trinity, as it shows God as three separate persons, yet one God. We donâ€™t have to fully understand this, but do have to accept it, as the Word says it is so. When we see Jesus face to face (1 Corinthians 13:12), and know all things, then we will fully understand many things that we now just have to accept by faith. In the book of Revelation it refers to the 7 Spirits of God (Revelation 4:5), so God must contain 7 Spirits. Praise God for His Word.
